messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] error installing 'unmarked'
parts:
Dear Paul,
 
I think mine was different, but I also had difficulties with installing the latest version of unmarked: as usual, I tried to install it from the internet directly and that seemed to work (i.e., R said the usual things about the md5 sums etc), but then when typing "library(unmarked)", unmarked couldn't be found by R. In the end I downloaded the zipped version and installed that successfully.
 
Not sure whether that helps.
 
Regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 3fcf0e009c95d23e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] error installing 'unmarked'
parts:
Hi Paul,

I haven't had the problem myself, but I saw that at least one person determined the problem was caused by another program locking the temporary files. In his case it was the antivirus software.  Temporarily disabling the software fixed the problem. Another person had the same problem, specifically after upgrading to Windows 7, with the same solution.

Good luck,

Chris Merkord
University of South Dakota

messages.author: b5151ca814beabec
messages.subject: Re: error installing 'unmarked'
parts:
HI,
I was able to install unmarked by finding the temporary location where RcppArmadillo had been placed and then 'manually' copying the RcppArmadillo folder from there to the R program files library (see first message below for location).  I'm not sure why the original unmarked install process was not able to carry this out.   I was not able to disable our antivirus software, so I could not try that suggested remedy.  I have now tested unmarked on several data sets I had used previously and it seems to work fine.  
 
Thanks for your help,
Paul Rasmussen
Wisconsin DNR
